<description>
Use of non-target directives is not recommended. As of CMake 4.5.0, it triggers `-Wnon-target-directive` warnings:
```console
$ cmake -B build -Wnon-target-directive
<snip>
CMake Warning (non-target-directive) at src/CMakeLists.txt:8 (include_directories):
  Use of non-target directives is not recommended.  Consider
  target_include_directories instead.
This warning is for project developers.  Use -Wno-author or
-Wno-non-target-directive to suppress it.

<snip>
```

Our custom [check](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/29f7e30d547c30ddb7a637bc3a2dbc7c0e3f5469/CMakeLists.txt#L744-L745) does not cover the `src/` subdirectory.

Once one of the CI jobs runs CMake >=4.5.0, that custom check can be removed.

The counterpart for the `secp256k1` repo is [here](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1996).
</description>

<commits>

Otherwise, `ipc/stub.cpp` is compiled without the project-wide

460f877fac cmake: Switch `include_directories` -> `target_include_directories`

Use of non-target directives is not recommended. As of CMake 4.5.0, it
triggers `-Wnon-target-directive` warnings.
